sketches: The k-Coloring dichotomy problem for H-free graphs (all k≥3, all H) contains as the k=3, H=P_t instance the question of the complexity of 3-colourability of P_t-free graphs.
The full k-Coloring dichotomy for H-free graphs (all k >= 3, all H) instantiated at k = 3 and H = P_t determines the complexity of 3-colourability of P_t-free graphs for every t >= 8.

source.name: k-Coloring dichotomy for H-free graphs
source.statement: For every integer $k \geq 3$, characterise the graphs $H$ for which the $k$-Coloring Problem restricted to $H$-free graphs is polynomial-time solvable versus NP-hard.
source.context: The paper observes that, in contrast with the List-$k$-Coloring Problem (now settled for all $k>4$), 'for the $k$-Coloring Problem, no value of $k\geq 3$ is known for which the "easy" choices of $H$ are completely distinguished from the "hard" ones.' This identifies a broad open problem motivating the paper's List-$k$-Coloring results.

target.name: 3-colourability complexity of P_t-free graphs
target.statement: Determine the complexity of $3$-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs for $t \geq 8$.
target.context: Polynomial-time algorithms for 3-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs are known for $t \leq 7$ (combining results for $t \leq 5$, $(k,t)=(3,7)$, and hardness for $P_7$-free graphs). The paper notes this problem remains open for $t \geq 8$, and provides a subexponential-time algorithm as partial progress.

sketches: Case (ii) with Δ_A=Δ_B=Δ and k_A=k_B=⌈C log Δ⌉ asserts every bipartite graph of maximum degree Δ is (k,k)-choosable, i.e. χ_ℓ(G) = O(log Δ), which is exactly the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture.

Case (ii) of the asymmetric conjecture with Δ_A=Δ_B=Δ and k_A=k_B=⌈C log Δ⌉ says every bipartite graph of maximum degree Δ is (⌈C log Δ⌉,⌈C log Δ⌉)-choosable, i.e. χ_ℓ(G) ≤ C log Δ + O(1), which is the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture.

Apply condition (ii) with Delta_A=Delta_B=Delta and k_A=k_B=ceil(C log Delta): the conjecture then says every bipartite graph of max degree Delta is (k_A,k_B)-choosable, i.e. chi_l(G) <= C log Delta + 1, which is the Alon-Krivelevich conjecture.

Condition (ii) of the source with Delta_A=Delta_B=Delta and k_A=k_B=ceil(C log Delta) asserts every bipartite graph of max degree Delta is (O(log Delta),O(log Delta))-choosable, i.e. chi_l <= c log Delta, the Alon-Krivelevich conjecture.

source.name: Asymmetric Krivelevich–Alon choosability for bipartite graphs
source.statement:
Let the positive integers $\Delta_A, \Delta_B, k_A, k_B$ satisfy one of the following.
(i) Given $\varepsilon > 0$, we have $\Delta_A, \Delta_B \geq \Delta_0$ for some $\Delta_0 = \Delta_0(\varepsilon)$, and $k_A \geq \Delta_A^\varepsilon$ and $k_B \geq \Delta_B^\varepsilon$.
(ii) For some absolute constant $C > 1$, $k_A \geq C \log \Delta_B$ and $k_B \geq C \log \Delta_A$.
(iii) $\Delta_A = \Delta_B = \Delta$, and, for some absolute constant $C > 0$, $k_B \geq C(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/k_A} \log\Delta$ or $k_A \geq C(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/k_B} \log\Delta$.
Then any bipartite graph $G = (V = A \cup B, E)$ with parts $A$ and $B$ having maximum degrees at most $\Delta_A$ and $\Delta_B$, respectively, is $(k_A, k_B)$-choosable.
source.context: Motivated by the asymptotic behaviour of $(k_A, k_B)$-choosability for complete bipartite graphs (Theorem 6 and Theorem 16), the authors conjecture three concrete asymmetric analogues of the Krivelevich–Alon conjecture. Condition (i) is weaker than Conjecture 2; conditions (ii) and (iii) are stronger. The paper shows Conjecture 7 holds for complete bipartite graphs (Theorem 15) and provides partial progress in the general case via Theorem 4 and its corollaries.

target.name: List chromatic number and maximum degree of bipartite graphs
target.statement: Conjecture There is a constant $ c $ such that the list chromatic number of any bipartite graph $ G $ of maximum degree $ \Delta $ is at most $ c \log \Delta $ .
target.context: For definitions and an introduction to list colouring, see the related Wikipedia page . Alon [A] showed that the list chromatic number of a graph (not necessarily bipartite) of maximum degree $ \Delta $ is at least $ \frac{1}{2}(1-o(1))\log_2\Delta $ . Random bipartite graphs show that this is tight up to a multiplicative factor $ (2+o(1)) $ . It is not diffcult to see that the list chromatic number of any bipartite graph $ G $ of maximum degree $ \Delta $ is at most $ O(\Delta/\log \Delta) $ . It also follows a more general result of Johansson [J] on triangle-free graphs.

sketches: Given min degree d, the conjecture yields either K_{x2(d)} (whose separation choosability grows with x2) or an induced bipartite subgraph of min degree x3(d), which by Esperet–Kang–Thomassé's theorem in the same paper has separation choosability Ω(log x3(d)); ch_sep is monotone under induced subgraphs (pad with fresh disjoint colors), so ch_sep(G)→∞ with d.

Stated in the paper: Conjecture 1.4 (clique K_{x2(d)} or induced bipartite subgraph of min degree x3(d)) implies Conjecture 1.3, since ch_sep(K_{d+1}) ~ √d (Kratochvíl–Tuza–Voigt) handles the clique outcome and Theorem 1.2 gives ch_sep lower bounds from dense induced bipartite subgraphs; both outcomes force ch_sep → ∞ with min degree.

source.name: Clique or dense bipartite subgraph in high-degree graphs
source.statement: There are functions $x_2(d)$ and $x_3(d)$ satisfying $x_2(d) \to \infty$ and $x_3(d) \to \infty$ as $d \to \infty$ such that any graph with minimum degree at least $d$ contains a complete subgraph on $x_2(d)$ vertices or a bipartite induced subgraph with minimum degree at least $x_3(d)$.
source.context: This conjecture, if true, would imply Conjecture 1.3: since $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(K_{d+1}) \sim \sqrt{d}$ (Kratochvíl–Tuza–Voigt) and Theorem 1.2 handles the dense bipartite induced subgraph case, the two alternatives together would give a separation-choosability lower bound tending to infinity for any graph of large minimum degree.

target.name: Separation choosability grows with minimum degree
target.statement: There is a function $x_1(d)$ that satisfies $x_1(d) \to \infty$ as $d \to \infty$ such that $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{sep}}(G) \geq x_1(d)$ for any graph $G$ with minimum degree $d$.
target.context: The authors prove Theorem 1.2 that separation choosability grows logarithmically in minimum degree for bipartite graphs, and ask whether the bipartiteness assumption can be dropped. The difficulty is that a bad list assignment with maximum separation on a graph does not necessarily retain maximum separation when edges are added, so the standard bipartite-subgraph reduction used for ordinary choosability fails.

sketches: A graph is 5-choosable iff it contains no subgraph critical for 5-choosability, and 5-colorable iff it contains no 6-critical subgraph. If on the torus these two families of critical graphs coincide, then a toroidal graph is 5-choosable iff it is 5-colorable.

A toroidal graph is not 5-choosable iff it contains a subgraph critical for 5-choosability, and not 5-colorable iff it contains a 6-critical subgraph. If the two families of critical graphs coincide on the torus, the two failure conditions coincide, so 5-choosable iff 5-colorable.

source.name: 5-choosability equals 6-criticality on torus
source.statement: A graph drawn on the torus is critical for 5-choosability if and only if it is $6$-critical.
source.context: Theorem 1 establishes this result under the additional assumption that there exists a cyclic system of non-contractible triangles around the torus with consecutive triangles at distance at most four. The authors verified that $K_7$ is the only graph critical for 5-list coloring but not for 5-choosability satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 1, and believe the cyclic system assumption can be dropped entirely.

target.name: 5-choosability equals 5-colorability on torus
target.statement: A toroidal graph is $5$-choosable if and only if it is $5$-colorable.
target.context: This conjecture is stated as equivalent to Conjecture 2 and represents the central goal of the paper: a complete choosability analogue of Thomassen's characterization of 5-colorability on the torus. The computational results of the paper, enumerating minimal obstructions under a cyclic-triangle-system condition, provide supporting evidence.
